# ProgressManager

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Progress.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Progress.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/interaction/physics-hold/Runtime/Scripts/Progress/ProgressManager.cs#L17)

The progress module: runs the scenario. Holds a queue of steps, hands the head of it its turn,
and advances when that step reports complete - so a scene plays out as a sequence rather than
as a set of components racing each other. Blocks can be queued at the front or at the back
while the run is going, which is how branching is done. Registers itself as
[`IProgressService`](/api/vrframework-core-runtime/IProgressService).

```csharp
public class ProgressManager : VRModule, IProgressService
```

### ClearPendingSteps() {#clearpendingsteps}

Drops everything the queue has lined up except the step running right now, so a block
enqueued next replaces the rest of the run instead of extending it.

```csharp
public void ClearPendingSteps()
```

### EnqueueBlock(ProgressBlock, bool) {#enqueueblock-progressblock-boolean}

Queues every step of a block, either behind everything already waiting or right after the step
running now - which is how a branch is taken without losing the rest of the run.

```csharp
public void EnqueueBlock(ProgressBlock block, bool end)
```

### OnNotifyStepComplete(ProgressStep) {#onnotifystepcomplete-progressstep}

Told by a step that it has finished: drops it from the queue, deactivates it and moves on to
the next. A step that is not in the queue is refused and logged.
